sources.entry: apscheduler - A light but powerful in-process task scheduler that lets you schedule functions.

summary.one_liner: APScheduler is a Python task scheduler and task queue library that runs functions on cron, interval, calendar, or one-off schedules, in-process or across multiple nodes.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes APScheduler as a task scheduler and task queue system for Python, usable purely as a job queue if scheduling is not needed. It offers synchronous (thread-based) and asynchronous (asyncio or Trio) flavors. Schedules and jobs can be persisted to PostgreSQL, MySQL and derivatives, SQLite, or MongoDB, so they survive restarts and can be shared between scheduler/worker instances. Multiple schedulers and workers can coordinate through event brokers listed as PostgreSQL, Redis, or MQTT. Built-in triggers cover cron-style, interval, calendar-based (every X years/months/weeks/days at a fixed time of day), and one-off runs, and triggers can be combined or replaced with custom trigger classes. It also supports limiting concurrent instances of a task, limiting how late a job may start, and adding jitter to run times. The README says documentation includes integration with WSGI or ASGI web applications.
use_cases: schedule Python functions to run periodically
cron-style jobs inside a Python application
distribute scheduled jobs across multiple nodes
persist scheduled tasks across process restarts
run background job queue in asyncio or Trio apps
schedule tasks within a Flask or Django-style WSGI/ASGI web app
notable: Synchronous and asynchronous (asyncio/Trio) variants in one library
Pluggable persistent data stores (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB)
Event brokers (PostgreSQL, Redis, MQTT) for multi-scheduler and multi-worker setups
Combining triggers and custom trigger classes
Jitter, max concurrent instances, and misfire/late-start limits
caveats: The v4.0 series is a pre-release that may change incompatibly without migration path; the README says not to use it in production
Multi-node setups require configuring a shared data store and event broker
keywords: schedule function once at specific time
